name: CIS Controls
full_name: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1 readiness: HCG control set organized by the 18 CIS Controls
issuing_body: Heights Consulting Group, organized on the CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1 (Center for Internet Security)
notice: HCG readiness control set organized by the 18 CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1. The names of the 18 Controls are taken from CIS's public list; the Safeguards, their numbering and the Implementation Group assignments are published by CIS under a non-commercial licence and are not reproduced. Controls here are HCG-written, carry HCG numbering, and note the lowest Implementation Group they correspond to.

sources.title: The 18 CIS Critical Security Controls (public list)
HCG CIS Controls readiness control set: controls, guidance and test points

control_flags.type: hcg for an HCG-written readiness control.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable controls implemented, with partial implementation counting as half. CIS defines no certification score; this percentage is an HCG readiness measure.

rules.summary: A control is implemented only when every HCG test point under it is met.

Controls apply according to the organization's target Implementation Group: an IG1 organization is assessed on controls marked IG1; IG2 adds those marked IG2; IG3 adds those marked IG3. Controls above the target group are marked not applicable.
rules.quote: The CIS Critical Security Controls (CIS Controls) are a prescriptive, prioritized, and simplified set of best practices

rules.summary: In the implementation score a partially implemented control counts as half. This is an HCG convention.

glossary.definition: A prioritized set of 18 cybersecurity controls published by the Center for Internet Security.
A specific action within a CIS Control. Version 8.1 has 153 Safeguards.

CIS's tiers for prioritizing Safeguards: IG1 is essential cyber hygiene for every organization, IG2 adds Safeguards for organizations with more complex IT, and IG3 adds Safeguards for organizations facing sophisticated attacks.
